 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed under Section 22 of Employees Compensation Act seeking compensation together with interest thereon at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of accident till the date of realization.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, father of petitioner No.1 to 3 i.e., one Siraj Khan (who herein after will be referred as deceased) was working as a driver in a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-0256 under respondent No.1 she is the wife of the deceased Siraj Khan.
It is submitted that as per the instruction of respondent No.1 on 13.05.2022 at 11.45 p.m, the deceased was drove the said lorry along with a load of Mangoes going from Bengaluru to Tirupati.

On 14.05.2022 at about 6.00 a.m, while he was proceeding near Toll Plaza on Puthkalapattu - Naidupeta NH-140 road, Pakala Mandal, suddenly deceased put the break of the lorry but he could not control over the vehicle and went to full left side of the road and dashed against the road side Toll plaza pole, from which the deceased was severely injured and died on spot.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to his family.
The family had conducted the last rites.
It is urged that prior to the accident the deceased was working as driver and drawing a salary of Rs.18,000/- per month and batta of Ra.300/- per day from respondent no.1.
The petitioners being the children of the deceased have suffered emotionally and financially from the death of the deceased.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the lorry and respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
As the accident took place during the course of employment, the respondents are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prayed to award compensation.

3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 appeared through her counsel and filed written statement admitting that as on the date of accident the deceased was working as a driver with her lorry and the accident occurred during the course of employment.

Further he admitted that she is the RC owner of the lorry bearing Reg.no.KA-06-AA-0256 and was duly insured with the 2nd respondent and same was in force further the driver of the lorry was having valid DL and the lorry possess valid FC and permit as on the date of accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing Reg.no.KA-06-AA-0256.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.1 has not complied with the provisions of Employees Act.

Further this respondent No.1 urged that there is no jural relationship of employer and employee Umme Hani.S vs Shamshad Khanum on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95434339/
2 between the deceased and respondent No.1.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
It is contended that the deceased alone responsible for the accident as he was not diligence in driving and due to his negligence accident took place.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the lorry / deceased did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
Further it is urged that as on the date of accident the insured lorry did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 13.05.2022 at about 11.45 p.m, the deceased was working as a driver under the respondent No.1's Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-06-AA-0256 and while discharging his duties the deceased met with an accident while he was proceeding near Toll Plaza on Puthakalapattu - Naidupete NH-140 road, Pakala Mandal, Chittor District, Andhra Pradesh.

Due to the said impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased died during the course of employment under the respondents?
3) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased?
4) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
5) What order or award?
6. Petitioner No.2 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 10 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager of respondent No.2 company as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 document.
7. Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record and arguments.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.5 : As per final order  for the following :

3  REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1:
It is the case of petitioners that, the deceased was working as a driver in a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-AA-0256 under respondent No.1 she is the wife of the deceased Siraj Khan.
It is submitted that as per the instruction of respondent No.1 on 13.05.2022 at 11.45 p.m, the deceased was drove the said lorry along with a load of Mangoes going from Bengaluru to Tirupati.

On 14.05.2022 at about 6.00 a.m, while he was proceeding near Toll Plaza on Puthkalapattu - Naidupeta NH-140 road, Pakala Mandal, suddenly deceased put the break of the lorry but he could not control over the vehicle and went to full left side of the road and dashed against the road side Toll plaza pole, from which the deceased was severely injured and died on spot.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to his family.
The family had conducted the last rites.
It is urged that prior to the accident the deceased was working as driver and drawing a salary of Rs.18,000/- per month and batta of Ra.300/- per day from respondent no.1.
The petitioners being the children of the deceased have suffered emotionally and financially from the death of the deceased.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the lorry and respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
As the accident took place during the course of employment, the respondents are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prayed to award compensation.
9. To substantiate the said fact, the petitioner No.2 got examined as PW-1 and produced documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.

P.6 . Ex.P.1 is the Certified copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the PM Report, Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.5 is the Charge sheet and Ex.P.6 is the Spot Mahazar,
Ex.P.7 to 9 are the Aadhar card, PAN card and Voter ID card of deceased and Ex.P.11 is the Ration card of petitioners No.1 to 3.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 got examined the Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 document.
10. This petition is filed under Section 22 of Employee's compensation Act 1923.

In the Employee compensation the injured or legal heirs of the deceased have to prove only the relationship between the employee and employer and the incident was occurred during the course of employment.

In this case, the contention of the petitioners that, the deceased was driver of the lorry under the respondent No.1 and incident was occurred at the time of employment as he was going along with a load of Mangoes and on 14.05.2022 at about 6.00 a.m, while he was proceeding near Toll Plaza on Puthakalapattu - Naidupeta NH-140 road, Pakala Mandal, suddenly the deceased put the break but he could not control over the vehicle and went to full left side of the road and dashed against the road side toll plaza pole and as a result he sustained grievous injuries and deceased died on the spot.
The respondent no.1 has not disputed that, the incident is occurred during the course of employment.
Further the respondent No.2 has also not disputed the incident.
After the incident the FIR was registered based on complaint and police have filed chargesheet as per Ex.P.5 as the accused died offence abated.
In a petition for compensation under the EC Act, negligence is not a material, the incident is sufficient.
In this case, the respondents have not all disputed the incident and death of the deceased in the accident.
Therefore without much discuss, this court answered the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

4 11.
ISSUE No.2 :

The petitioners contended that prior to the accident the deceased was working as driver under the respondent No.1 and drawing a salary of Rs.18,000/- per month and batta of Ra.300/- per day and died during the course of employment.

The respondent no.1 owner of the lorry appeared and filed written statement clearly admitted that, at the time of accident, the deceased was working as a driver and further admitted that she is the wife of the deceased.

The respondent No.2 insurance company has disputed the claim petition of the petitioners as the deceased is the husband of the respondent No.1 and they are husband and wife, therefore there is no relationship as employee and employer between the deceased and the respondent No.1.
Therefore contended that the claim petition against them is not maintainable.
12. The respondent No.2 examined its Manager as RW1 and produced Ex.R.1 copy of insurance policy.
He completely supported the case of the respondent No.2 during his chief- examination.
When he was subjected to the litmus test of cross- examination he categorically admitted that the policy was in force as on date of accident.
He further admitted that the company had get investigated through its internal agency.
Further he has also admitted that he has not produced any documents before the court.
When such being the case mere self proclaimed and self centric statement of RW1 cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.
Further he categorically admitted that there is no specific condition in their policy about husband and wife having employer and employee relationship.

Under these circumstances they have no right to take contention stating that, the deceased is the husband of respondent No.1 and they are husband and wife, therefore there is no relationship between the deceased and respondent No.1 as employee and employer.

13. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Madras in CMA.No.1651/2017 and CMP.No.8760/2017 in the case of M/s United India Insurance Company Limited V/s Thirumati. Saraswathi and others wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Madras Observed that, the husband and wife may be an employer and employee in certain cases.

entities.text: M/s United India Insurance Company Limited V/s Thirumati. Saraswathi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
the factum of the relationship between employer and employee is to be establish with some principles and evidence.
Mere statement that the husband was working as a lorry cleaner with his wife is insufficient to arrive conclusion that employer and employee relationship exist between the husband and wife.

Hon'ble High Court relied on the observations made in the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Gottumukkala Appala Narasimharaju v/s National Insurance Co.Ltd. reported in 2013 SC 446 and contended that the relationship between the husband and wife is to be established through the acceptable evidence and by establishing the fact beyond any pale of doubt and allow the appeal filed by the insurance company.

entities.text: Gottumukkala Appala Narasimharaju v/s National Insurance Co.Ltd. reported in 2013 SC 446
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. In the present case on hand the advocate for petitioners argued that admittedly there is no condition in the policy about husband and wife are father and son could not be a employer and employee.
In a family business it is quite common that to engage their own family employer for doing business.
In such situation it is difficult to maintain the documentary evidences.
If a businesses are very big scale businesses then they can maintain documents even employment between the relationship in family business.
If a businesses are small scale then it is difficult to maintain the documentary evidences.
In the present case, there was small scale business, the respondent No.1 has having a lorry and appointed her husband as a driver and also looking to the business.
In such circumstances no documentary evidences are available.

Therefore, considering the Umme Hani.S vs Shamshad Khanum on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95434339/
5 same he sought for allow the petition.

He relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in case of Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Hanumantha and another reported in 2006 ACJ 251, wherein Honb'el High Court of Karnataka held that :
"2. The contention of the insurer that there exists no relationship of employer (driver) happens to be the son of the owner of the jeep, respondent No. 2, therefore,
there cannot be a relationship of employer and employee is an untenable argument.
It is not uncommon amongst the business family to engage their own kith and kin on employment for doing the business or commercial activity.

entities.text: Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Hanumantha and another reported in 2006 ACJ 251
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely because in such a situation no wages are paid in cash is also not a ground to infer absence of a legal relationship of employer and employee, since there would always be consideration in kind computable in terms of money for the services rendered.

The parties https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis/ C.M.A.No.1651 of 2017 and would not go for documentation of the contract nor create any documentary material to prove payment of wages in view of the peculiar family relationship.

Therefore, the fact that the respondent No. 1 and respondent No. 2 are father and son, is not a ground in law to infer the absence of the relationship of employer and employee under Workmen's Compensation Act."
15.

On the other hand it is relevant to rely on the decisions :
1) MFA No.31321/2010 (WC) (Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited V.s Smt.Pramilabai and others) "The fact that the driver and cleaner are having blood relationship would not be a reason to suspect the employer and employee relationship between the son and the father and there is no such impediment in law to employ the family member as an employee by the employer."

2. 2006 (1) KCCR 588 (The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited V/s.
Yallappa Bhimappa Alagudi and another) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - Section 166 - Authorized Agent - The concept of relationship of master and servant should not be understood in its literal sense - Anybody doing gratuitously for the owner is deemed to be an authorized agent and the concept of master and servant relationship gets invoked.

It is not uncommon that the family members are employed in the course of business.
The fact that the family members are not regularly employed and that no wages are paid is not valid reason to defeat the case of relationship of master and servant.

ACJ 519 (Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., V/s. Ramesh and another) "Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, Section 22 and Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 147 - Claim application - Employer-employee relationship - Motor Insurance - Liability of insurance company

yes." 
16. In view of the above decisions, it make clears that the husband is the employee under his wife.
Further, at this juncture I would like to refer the Sec.2(dd) & (e) of Employee's compensation act 1923.

2. Definitions. - (1) In this Act unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context - (dd) "employee" means a person, who is - (i) a railway servant as defined in clause (34) of Section 2 of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989), no permanently employed in any administrative district or sub-divisional office of a railway and not employed in any such capacity as is specified in Schedule II; or (ii) (a) a master, seaman or other member of the crew of a ship,
(b) a captain or other member of the crew of an aircraft,
(c) a person recruited as driver, helper, mechanic, cleaner or in any other capacity in connection with a motor vehicle,
(d) a person recruited for work aborad by a company, and who is employed outside India in any such capacity as is specified in Schedule II and the ship, aircraft or motor vehicle, or company, as the case may be, is registered in India; or (iii) employed in any such capacity as is specified in Schedule II, whether the contract of employment was made before or after the passing of this Act and whether such contract is expressed or implied, oral or in writing; but does not include any person working in the capacity of a member of the Armed Forces of the Union; and any reference to any employee who has been injured shall,
where the employee is dead, include a reference to his dependents or any of them;
Sec.2 (e) -employee includes any body of persons whether incorporation or not and any managing agent of an employer and the legal representative of a deceased employer, and, when the services of a employee are temporarily lent or let on hire to another person by the person with whom the employee has entered into a contract of service or apprenticeship, means such other person while the employee is working for him."
17.
The Sec.2(dd) of EC Act clearly says that whether such contract express or implied, oral or in writing.
Therefore though the respondent No.1 and deceased are wife and husband, but admittedly Umme Hani.

7
the deceased was working as a driver on Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-0256.

The respondent No.2 has contended in objection as it is submitted by the respondent no.2 that, only an employee who is an authorized by the insured alone can drive vehicle as driver, then only there is a vicarious act.
In this case, though respondent No.1 is wife of deceased, she had authorized the deceased as driver to the her vehicle, then deceased was the employee.
Therefore when he was working as a driver it is implied either oral contract between the respondent No.1 and deceased with their employment.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka clearly held that, it may be possible that the husband is employee under the wife.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 is the owner of the Lorry.
If the husband of the respondent No.1 is not worked as a driver, certainly the respondent No.1 engaged the separate driver as her employee and pay the payment.

Here the respondent No.1 engaged/appoint her husband as driver to her lorry it is an implied contract stated under the 2(dd)
of EC Act.
Further there is no bar in the provisions of EC act to appoint the husband or relative their employee.

Therefore the contention raised by the respondent No.2 as the deceased is the husband of the respondent No.1 and they are husband and wife, therefore there is no relationship as employee and employer cannot be accepted.
Admittedly the deceased was doing driving work on the offending vehicle as a driver and he died on duty.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to disbelieved the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.

Therefore with these discussion and principle held above, this court is of the opinion that, there is a relationship between the deceased and the respondent No.1 as an employee and employer and the death was occurred during the course of employment.
Hence, this court answers the issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.3 :- This issue is pertaining to whether the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card, PAN Card and Election ID card of deceased and ration card of petitioners through PW-1 as per Ex.P.7 to 10.
The respondents have not disputed as the petitioners are legal heirs of deceased.
Therefore on perusal of these documents, it established that, the petitioners are legal heirs of deceased and they contended that, they are the dependents to the deceased.
Admittedly the petitioners are children of deceased.
Therefore naturally they are dependents on the deceased.
Hence, this court answer this issue in the Affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.4 :
As discussed in the issue No.1 to 3 and reasons stated therein, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled compensation.
Now the question is what is the compensation amount and who is liable to pay the compensation ?.
20. The petitioners have got exhibited the Aadhar card and PAN Card of the deceased which is marked as Ex.P7 & 8 wherein his year of date of birth is reflected as 14.07.1965.
This indicates that he was aged 56 years on the date of accident.
21. The petitioners have claimed the compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12%.
The petitioners contended that, the deceased was a driver and earning of Rs.18,000/-p.m. and Rs.300/- Batta per day.
But the petitioners have not produced any documents with respect to the salary of deceased.
The petitioners did not made any endevour to produce the bank statement of the deceased or any such other documents.

Hence reliance is placed on the Gazette Notification dated 03.01.2020 issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment which Umme Hani.S vs Shamshad Khanum on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95434339/
8 reads as under :
S.O. 71(E).-In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1B) of section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923) and in supersession of the notification of the Ministry of Labour and Employment issued vide number S.O.
1258(E), dated 31st May, 2010 ;

published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii), dated 31st May, 2010, the Central Government hereby specifies, for the purposes of sub-section (1) of the said section, the following amount as monthly wages, with effect from the date of publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, namely:-
"Fifteen thousand rupees"
Accordingly
the income of deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/- per month.

As per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased employee shall be an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the said employee multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, whichever is more.
50% of Rs.15,000/- works out to Rs.7,500/-.
Relevant factor is 131.95.
Hence, compensation payable to the petitioners would be Rs.7,500 x 131.95 = Rs.9,89,625/- which is rounded off to Rs.9,90,000/-.
Further the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased.

22. The calculation table stands as follows:

Compensation for the : 9,90,000-00 death of the deceased 2 Funeral expenses of the : 16,500-00 deceased Total 10,06,500-00 23.
INTEREST & LIABILITY :

Relying upon the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in AIR 2014 SUPREME COURT 1393 (Saberabibi Yakubbhai Saikh vs. National insurance Co Ltd., and others), this court hold that the petitioners are entitled for interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of incident i.e., 13.05.2022 till the date of realization.

sentences.text: 24. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 12% p.a., from the date of the incident till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this court is answered Issue No.4 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
25. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed u/s.22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 30%

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts: The respondent No.1 has not complied with the provisions of Employees Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 13.05.2022 at about 11.45 p.m, the deceased was working as a driver under the respondent No.1's Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-06-AA-0256 and while discharging his duties the deceased met with an accident while he was proceeding near Toll Plaza on Puthakalapattu - Naidupete NH-140 road, Pakala Mandal, Chittor District, Andhra Pradesh.
Due to the said impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased died during the course of employment under the respondents?
3) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased?
4) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
5) What order or award?
Now the question is what is the compensation amount and who is liable to pay the compensation ?.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the Employee compensation the injured or legal heirs of the deceased have to prove only the relationship between the employee and employer and the incident was occurred during the course of employment.
In this case, the contention of the petitioners that, the deceased was driver of the lorry under the respondent No.1 and incident was occurred at the time of employment as he was going along with a load of Mangoes and on 14.05.2022 at about 6.00 a.m, while he was proceeding near Toll Plaza on Puthakalapattu - Naidupeta NH-140 road, Pakala Mandal, suddenly the deceased put the break but he could not control over the vehicle and went to full left side of the road and dashed against the road side toll plaza pole and as a result he sustained grievous injuries and deceased died on the spot.
The respondent no.1 has not disputed that, the incident is occurred during the course of employment.
Further the respondent No.2 has also not disputed the incident.
After the incident the FIR was registered based on complaint and police have filed chargesheet as per Ex.P.5 as the accused died offence abated.
In a petition for compensation under the EC Act, negligence is not a material, the incident is sufficient.
In this case, the respondents have not all disputed the incident and death of the deceased in the accident.
When such being the case mere self proclaimed and self centric statement of RW1 cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.
In the present case, there was small scale business, the respondent No.1 has having a lorry and appointed her husband as a driver and also looking to the business.
In such circumstances no documentary evidences are available.
2. 2006 (1) KCCR 588 (The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited V/s.
Yallappa Bhimappa Alagudi and another) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - Section 166 - Authorized Agent - The concept of relationship of master and servant should not be understood in its literal sense - Anybody doing gratuitously for the owner is deemed to be an authorized agent and the concept of master and servant relationship gets invoked.
ACJ 519 (Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., V/s. Ramesh and another) "Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, Section 22 and Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 147 - Claim application - Employer-employee relationship - Motor Insurance - Liability of insurance company
Therefore though the respondent No.1 and deceased are wife and husband, but admittedly Umme Hani.
In this case, though respondent No.1 is wife of deceased, she had authorized the deceased as driver to the her vehicle, then deceased was the employee.
Therefore when he was working as a driver it is implied either oral contract between the respondent No.1 and deceased with their employment.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 is the owner of the Lorry.
If the husband of the respondent No.1 is not worked as a driver, certainly the respondent No.1 engaged the separate driver as her employee and pay the payment.
Here the respondent No.1 engaged/appoint her husband as driver to her lorry it is an implied contract stated under the 2(dd)
of EC Act.
Further there is no bar in the provisions of EC act to appoint the husband or relative their employee.
Admittedly the deceased was doing driving work on the offending vehicle as a driver and he died on duty.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to disbelieved the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.

Under these circumstances they have no right to take contention stating that, the deceased is the husband of respondent No.1 and they are husband and wife, therefore there is no relationship between the deceased and respondent No.1 as employee and employer.

Saraswathi and others wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Madras Observed that, the husband and wife may be an employer and employee in certain cases.
In a family business it is quite common that to engage their own family employer for doing business.
If a businesses are very big scale businesses then they can maintain documents even employment between the relationship in family business.
If a businesses are small scale then it is difficult to maintain the documentary evidences.
opennyai_summary.decision:
21. The petitioners have claimed the compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12%.
Hence reliance is placed on the Gazette Notification dated 03.01.2020 issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment which Umme Hani.S vs Shamshad Khanum on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95434339/
8 reads as under :
S.O. 71(E).-In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1B) of section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923) and in supersession of the notification of the Ministry of Labour and Employment issued vide number S.O.
1258(E), dated 31st May, 2010 ;
published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii), dated 31st May, 2010, the Central Government hereby specifies, for the purposes of sub-section (1) of the said section, the following amount as monthly wages, with effect from the date of publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, namely:-
"Fifteen thousand rupees"
Accordingly
the income of deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/- per month.
As per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased employee shall be an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the said employee multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, whichever is more.
50% of Rs.15,000/- works out to Rs.7,500/-.
Relevant factor is 131.95.
Hence, compensation payable to the petitioners would be Rs.7,500 x 131.95 = Rs.9,89,625/- which is rounded off to Rs.9,90,000/-.
Further the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased.
Compensation for the : 9,90,000-00 death of the deceased 2 Funeral expenses of the : 16,500-00 deceased Total 10,06,500-00 23.
INTEREST & LIABILITY :
24. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 12% p.a., from the date of the incident till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this court is answered Issue No.4 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
25. ISSUE NO.5:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed u/s.22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
Umme Hani
Shamshad Khanum
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,06,500/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of incident till its realization.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 30%
 Petitioner No.2 - 40%
 Petitioner No.3 - 30%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
